version.value: Beach’s Browning setting, recorded as the second song on a single-faced 10-inch side, after Frank La Forge’s “How Much I Love You”
version.note: The label lists both songs, (a) La Forge and (b) Beach. The key sung and any cuts or changes to the printed song are not established.

performers.note: The label reads ‘Soprano with pianoforte’ and names Johanna Gadski; the Discography of American Historical Recordings names La Forge as pianist.

date.note: Matrix B-5018, take 2; the date is also handwritten on the label.

place.value: New York, New York, United States
place.note: Recording place from the Discography of American Historical Recordings; no studio address is given.

label.value: Victor Talking Machine Company, Red Seal

catalogue.note: Listed on the Gadski page of the Victor catalogue of July 1909.

matrixTakeSides.note: Take 1 was held; take 2 was the master issued as 87026.

credits.value: Library of Congress Packard Campus for Audio Visual Conservation; National Jukebox MP3 mirrored by Hessel Digital Library
credits.note: Credits as stated in the Internet Archive item, which links to the National Jukebox record and notes Sony Music Entertainment or EMI Music as the source of the disc.

date.note: The digitisation date is not given. The mirror was added to the Internet Archive on 18 October 2026, a copying event.

processing.note: Playback speed, stylus, equalisation and noise reduction are not stated. A separate Great 78 Project transfer of the same disc is about seven per cent longer, so the speed of the Library’s copy is not certain.

digital.format: VBR MP3 mirror of a Library of Congress National Jukebox disc transfer

composition.value: Out of copyright: Beach died in 1944, Browning in 1889 and La Forge in 1953.
composition.note: Life-plus-70 terms have run out for all three; the 1900 edition was published in the United States. This covers the historical songs, not modern editions.

recording.value: US public domain: first published 1908 or 1909 on Victor 87026; the mirror carries the Public Domain Mark.
recording.note: Selected under the project’s us-published-before-cutoff rule. The July 1909 Victor catalogue lists the disc; the Library of Congress gives 1908. The Public Domain Mark is a status declaration, not a new licence.
